Performance benchmarks ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate N minimal JSONL sessions in a temp directory.\nfn generate_sessions(dir: &Path, count: usize) {\n    for i in 0..count {\n        let session_id = format!(\"perf-session-{:04}\", i);\n        let content = format!(\n            \"{}\\n{}\\n\",\n            serde_json::json!({\n                \"type\": \"user\",\n                \"uuid\": format!(\"u{}-1\", i),\n                \"sessionId\": session_id,\n                \"timestamp\": \"2024-01-15T10:00:00Z\",\n                \"cwd\": format!(\"/home/user/project-{}\", i % 10),\n                \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n                \"message\": {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": format!(\"Fix the bug in module {}\", i)}\n            }),\n            serde_json::json!({\n                \"type\": \"assistant\",\n                \"uuid\": format!(\"u{}-2\", i),\n                \"sessionId\": session_id,\n                \"timestamp\": \"2024-01-15T10:00:30Z\",\n                \"cwd\": format!(\"/home/user/project-{}\", i % 10),\n                \"message\": {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": format!(\"I'll fix the bug in module {}. The issue is a missing null check.\", i)}\n            })\n        );\n        let file_path = dir.join(format!(\"{}.jsonl\", session_id));\n        fs::write(&file_path, content).expect(\"failed to write session\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// Scraping 1000 minimal sessions must complete within 300 seconds.\n#[test]\nfn test_scrape_1000_sessions_under_60s() {\n    let data_dir = make_data_dir();\n    let [`LogFormat`] specifies which\n225\t/// parser to use for a given plugin. The format determines:\n226\t///\n227\t/// - How the file is read (streaming vs. random access)\n228\t/// - How sessions are detected (one-file-per-session vs. delimiters vs. queries)\n229\t/// - What fields are available for mapping\n230\t/// - Whether incremental scraping is supported\n231\t///\n232\t/// # Format Variants\n233\t///\n234\t/// ## Jsonl\n235\t/// **Best for**: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode (legacy), Pi, Goose\n236\t///\n237\t/// JSONL (JSON Lines) format: one JSON object per line. Supports incremental scraping via\n238\t/// byte offset tracking. Each line can represent an event, session metadata, or noise.\n239\t/// Requires envelope unwrapping for formats like Codex where lines are wrapped in\n240\t/// `{timestamp, type, payload}` structures.\n241\t///\n242\t/// ## Markdown\n243\t/// **Best for**: Aider\n244\t///\n245\t/// Plain text Markdown with delimiter-based session detection. Sessions are separated by\n246\t/// marker lines (e.g., `# aider chat started at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`). Incremental\n247\t/// scraping tracks the last delimiter position to handle partially-written sessions.\n248\t///\n249\t/// ## JsonTree\n250\t/// **Best for**: OpenCode (current), some legacy Codex formats\n251\t///\n252\t/// Hierarchical JSON files where sessions, messages, and parts are stored in separate\n253\t/// files or database tables. Requires tree traversal and re-assembly to extract events\n254\t/// in conversation order.\n255\t///\n256\t/// ## Sqlite\n257\t/// **Best for**: Cursor, Windsurf\n258\t///\n259\t/// SQLite databases where sessions and messages are stored in tables. Requires SQL\n260\t/// queries with row ordering to extract events. Supports incremental scraping via\n261\t/// time-based filtering (`time_updated > last_scraped`).\n262\t///\n263\t/// ## JsonArray\n264\t/// **Best for**: Gemini CLI\n265\t///\n266\t/// Single JSON file containing an array of message objects. The entire file is read\n267\t/// into memory and parsed as an array. Does not support incremental scraping via byte\n268\t/// offsets (the array is rewritten in place), so falls back to mtime-based full rescans.\n269\t///\n270\t/// # Choosing a Format\n271\t///\n272\t/// When authoring custom plugins, choose the format that matches the agent's native storage:\n273\t///\n274\t/// - Agent writes line-by-line to a file → `Jsonl` (most Plugins are TOML files stored in `~/.agentscribe/plugins/` with the `.toml` extension.\n//! Each plugin defines a [`Plugin`] struct with three main sections:\n//!\n//! ```toml\n//! [parser]\n//! timestamp = \"timestamp\"\n//! role = \"message.role\"\n//! content = \"message.content\"\n//! ```\n//!\n//! # Bundled Plugins\n//!\n//! AgentScribe ships with plugins for:\n//! - **Claude Code** (`claude-code.toml`) - JSONL format with session metadata files\n//! - **Aider** (`aider.toml`) - Markdown format with delimiter-based session detection\n//! - **OpenCode** (`opencode.toml`) - SQLite format with JSON tree extraction\n//! - **Codex** (`codex.toml`) - JSONL format with envelope unwrapping\n//! - **Cursor** (`cursor.toml`) - SQLite format with KV store extraction\n//! - **Windsurf** (`windsurf.toml`) - SQLite format similar to Cursor\n//!\n//! # Custom Plugins\n//!\n//! Users can add custom plugins by dropping TOML files in `~/.agentscribe/plugins/`.\n//! See `plugins/BUILDING_PLUGINS.md` for the complete plugin authoring guide.\n//!\n//! # Validation\n//!\n//! Plugins are validated at load time for:\n//! - Required fields (name, version, paths, format)\n//! - Valid format values (jsonl, markdown, json-tree, sqlite, json-array)\n//! - Valid session detection methods for the chosen format\n//! - Valid envelope routing actions (event, meta, skip)\n//! - Path expansion and accessibility\n//!\n//!
